key_insight: Deterministic geometric environments provide unambiguous, physics-grounded signals that let 3D spatial reasoning models self-generate corrective supervision—enabling models to evolve without reinforcing their own geometric errors.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on costly geometric annotation and overcomes the self-supervised pitfall where model-consensus pseudo-labeling amplifies existing spatial errors in continual/self-evolving training.
method: Create deterministic geometric environments/simulators that yield analytically computable ground-truth spatial relations and constraints.

Run an iterative self-evolving loop: synthesize scenes, let the model predict, apply environment-derived geometric checks and deterministic transforms to detect and correct erroneous pseudo-labels, then retrain.
Use physics- and geometry-based filtering (not model consensus) to select high-quality pseudo-labels and progressively expand training data for continual improvement.
impact: Enables scalable, low-cost continual improvement of embodied spatial intelligence, improving robustness and generalization for robotics, AR/VR, and 3D perception applications without extensive manual annotation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: deterministic scene generator → model prediction → geometry-based validation/correction → model update (self-evolving loop).
Before/after scene examples highlighting corrected spatial errors (e.g., object placement, occlusion, depth) after evolution.
Schematic of deterministic geometric checks (ray intersections, analytic constraints, conserved quantities) illustrating how ground-truth is derived.
Performance-over-iterations chart showing steady improvement without human labels (iteration vs. spatial accuracy).
paper_title: SpatialEvo: Self-Evolving Spatial Intelligence via Deterministic Geometric Environments
paper_authors: Dinging Li, Yingxiu Zhao, Xinrui Cheng, Kangheng Lin, Hongbo Peng
